2158. Calculating nCr Using a Factorial Function

90

Hard

Problem Statement
Read n and r and print the value of nCr (the number of ways to choose r items from n items), by calling a factorial function more than once.

Description
The number of ways to choose r items from n items is given by nCr = n! / (r! x (n - r)!). Read two integers n and r from input. Write a function factorial that takes an integer parameter and uses a for loop to return its factorial (the factorial of 0 is 1). In main(), call this one function three times, for n, for r, and for n - r, and use the results to calculate and print nCr.
input_spec:
. Write a function factorial that takes an integer parameter and uses a for loop to return its factorial (the factorial of 0 is 1). In main(), call this one function three times, for n, for r, and for n - r, and use the results to calculate and print nCr.

Input Description
Two integers n and r separated by a space (0 <= r <= n <= 10).
